title: Lint --fix through the compile gate
summary: lint --fix --apply --project X.dproj goes through the compile gate by default (1.51): an error stops or rolls back the fix; new warnings / hints are reported
intro: Read this before letting lint --fix write into a project you cannot afford to break. When --project names an existing .dproj the project builds before and after the write (the default since 1.51; --compile-gate forces it, --no-compile-gate opts out except for naming renames). An error in build 1 stops the run, an error in build 2 rolls every file back, and stderr lists the counts of both builds, every error line and the warnings / hints the fix added.

help:
drag-lint lint --in --fix [--fix-line --fix-rule ] [--fix-naming] [--apply [--no-backup]] [--project [--compile-gate | --no-compile-gate] [--platform

] [--rsvars ] [--build-timeout ]] (AUTOFIX one file; --apply keeps a .bak beside each file it writes unless --no-backup)

questions.ask: How do I make lint --fix check that the project still builds?
